entries.title: Remaining leads from the survey of comparable agent orchestrators (Oct 2026)
entries.body:
Leads borrowed from comparable open-source agent orchestrators, surveyed in October 2026 (first imported from issue #671).
Nothing here is a commitment; these are leads to triage.
The orch checked each against the code on 2026-11-17: ideas lym has built or that proved moot are dropped,
partly built ones name only what is still open, and the eight most worth doing are notes of their own in this project.
Each bullet names its source project and the lym module it would touch.

## Plan validation and concurrency (quarry, Plan-Write, board)

- **Typed scope operations on cards** (foremerge): each scope carries an additive or breaking operation,
  and deterministic rules flag colliding pairs even when files do not overlap.
  Worth comparing against board labels and the alignment gate.
- **Symbol leases between concurrent tasks** (Fusion, ORCH): expiring leases on symbol keys serialize overlapping tasks,
  with a deterministic tie-break; lym keeps overlapping tasks apart by board labels.
- **Commit-time reservation guard** (ntm): a pre-commit hook refuses a commit touching what another task holds; needs leases first.
- **Criterion amendment ledger** (oh-my-claudecode): a card's acceptance text changes only through a recorded amendment in weft.

## Review (burler, Bouncer)

- **Quorum of differently-angled judges** (ccswarm): lym fans out lenses but has no quorum vote for high-risk segments.
  Since 2026-11-19 a run's parent orch can be asked to see and veto each Code-Review round and each drift judge ruling
  (`code_review_ask_parent`, `judge_ask_parent`); that is one extra judge, not a quorum.
- **Risk tier by changed paths** (yylo): globs over sensitive paths choose the review depth and the gate scope.

## Engine, recipes and governance (shed, tender, orch, board)

- **Cross-run quarantine** (Bernstein): a task that fails three times across runs is held, unless the failures were the host's.
- **Fork a run from a step with a tree snapshot** (Bernstein): `shed goto` moves the cursor but does not restore the warp tree.
- **Warm retry guarded by a workspace hash** (Bernstein): resume the native session only when the tree is unchanged.
- **Evidence reuse by input identity** (yylo): verify is skipped on the same tree; a changed review prompt could rerun only the review.
- **Guidance at the next step boundary** (Conductor): a queue of operator guidance for the next producer's prompt.
  Partly met since 2026-11-19: `notify_parent_on` in `loom.yaml` mails the run's parent when a named row is reached,
  so the parent can brief that row's agent as it starts; there is still no queue of guidance lym itself folds into the prompt.
- **Batched operator questions with recorded assumptions** (Spec Kit `/clarify`, Conductor): Discussion-Write asks at most a few ranked questions,
  each with a recommended answer, and records unanswered ones as assumptions.
  Since 2026-11-19 a run's autonomous agents put their questions to the run's parent orch, not to the operator in their pane;
  Discussion, which the operator sits in, still asks in its pane, so this lead concerns Discussion only.
- **Rate-limit wait**: the orch watcher wakes the orch after a usage reset; tender itself schedules no resume.
- **Standing goals and scheduled routines** (ORCH, CAO, Fusion): periodic triage, dependency bumps or `selfreport` sweeps.

## Agent sessions (reed, shuttle)

- **Waiting-for-input signal** (agent-of-empires): shuttle has an awaiting-input state; screen heuristics still decide readiness and startup.
- **Reference status patterns and a paste pitfall** (CAO): compare its regexes and its tmux bracketed-paste note with shuttle's readiness and creel inject.
- **Context forecasting** (ntm): the orch cycles its context; Webster's Master and the loom driver do not, and nothing forecasts.
- **Staggered spawns** (ntm): space Webster forks and batten fan-out by learned rate limits.

## Observability (report, weft)

- **Hash-chained run journal** (Bernstein): a hash chain over producer outputs makes an archived run self-verifying.
- **Unverified-completion rate** (Bernstein): a `lym report` view of completions with no test or gate behind them.
- **Commit-to-record links** (AgentNote): weft links to warp by a `Warp-SHA:` trailer; a note or trailer on each warp commit could link back.
- **Run diff** (ccswarm): `lym report` comparing two archived runs' timelines and token use.
- **OpenTelemetry spans per producer** (Conductor).

## Operator attention (orch, dobby, reed)

- **Attention feed with acknowledgement states** (ntm): dobby's wait reminders have no seen, snoozed or acknowledged states.

## Discussion review (Discussion-Write, stencils, pattern)

- **Requirements-quality checklist** (Spec Kit `/checklist`): items with IDs the Discussion-review judge answers one by one.
- **Fixed analysis categories** (Kiro): inconsistency, ambiguity, conflicts, unstated assumptions and missing edge cases as named lenses.
- **PATTERN rules handed to reviewers** (Spec Kit constitution): its rules as numbered MUSTs in plan and code review prompts.
- **Glob-scoped steering** (Kiro): stencils pull per-area guidance chosen by the paths of a plan's glyphs.

entries.title: A closed area for lym: bwrap sandbox in stages, off by default
entries.brief: Run the lym process tree in a bwrap area with a host proxy and broker, built in three stages with a stop; to be split if it goes ahead
entries.body:
## Seen (operator, 2026-10-30)

Every agent lym starts runs with `--dangerously-skip-permissions`, which many people do not accept, and a repository that states it supports safe sandboxing is worth more than one that does not.
The operator uses lym alone, on Linux (OSL-1046: Ubuntu 24.04; Neve: Kubuntu on Ubuntu 26.04, Plasma 6), and has no interest in other users or in Windows.
The research is `docs/research/platform/sandboxing-options-2026-10-30.md`: it weighs `bwrap`, Landlock, a dedicated Linux user, systemd sandboxing, podman and Claude Code's own `/sandbox`, and the packages and cards each would change.

Two exposures hold today with no area: an agent can reach `/run/user/<uid>/bus` and through it `systemd-run --user`, which starts any process outside lym's tree, and it can type into other hubs' tmux panes through their sockets in `/tmp/tmux-<uid>`, the Models hub's among them.

## Idea

Run the whole lym process tree inside a `bwrap` area launched by lym itself, with the agents free inside it and a short, controlled list of exits.
It is an option the operator turns on, never a requirement: with it off, everything works as it does today, and with it on, nothing starts when the sandbox cannot.
The operator thinks the full design is complicated and error-prone, and doubts it will work without large problems, so it is built in stages with a stop between them.
This is one large note and is split into tasks, or a project, only when the operator decides it goes ahead.

### Before the area: two cheap steps

- Start a hub's tmux server from a Konsole window, not a VS Code terminal: the server inherits the `vscode` AppArmor profile, which grants user namespaces to every agent of the hub.
- A line in `README.md` that every agent lym starts runs with bypass permissions, and that lym belongs on a machine the operator is willing to hand to its agents.

### Stage 1: the filesystem area only

`bwrap` with `--unshare-all --die-with-parent --clearenv` around reed's tmux server and everything under it, started by a new `lym area start` and a supervisor inside.

- The hub is bound read-write at its own path, since the tmux server name, the creel socket name, git's worktree links and Claude Code's transcript directory all derive from absolute paths; `/usr`, `/etc` and `/opt` are read-only, `$HOME` a tmpfs with read-only binds of the Go toolchain, the Claude Code binary and the installed `lym`.
- The area has its own Claude config directory and Go caches bound at the usual paths, with the host's plugin cache read-only on top, so the host's `settings.json` hooks never run in it.
- One host directory holds the tmux socket directory, so `lym reed attach` from outside drives the server inside; tried on OSL-1046 with a tmux server inside `bwrap`.
- `.git/hooks` is read-only; `.git/config` was to stay writable for `branch.<b>.lymLocal`, but `fabric-remote-async` removed that mark and `internal/gitrepo/branchmark.go`, so the reason is gone; whether git itself or another lym writer still needs `.git/config` writable is unchecked.
- Network stays open and there is no broker, so the landing deploy, `lym reed window`, `lym ide` and `lym hibernate request` do not work from inside; the operator does them by hand, from outside.
- A config module `area` with `required`, off by default; `lym area start` refuses on any failure and never falls back to an unsandboxed start.
- Ubuntu 24.04 needs a one-time AppArmor profile for `/usr/bin/bwrap`, loaded by root; the report names the profile, and Ubuntu 25.04 and later ship it, which is not verified on Neve.

This closes the two exposures above and shows early whether tmux, creel and dobby run well inside an area.

### Stop: the operator decides whether stage 1 works well enough to go on.

### Stage 2: egress through a host proxy

No network inside the area; a host-side proxy, reached through a bound socket, allows CONNECT to `api.anthropic.com`, `claude.ai`, `platform.claude.com`, `proxy.golang.org`, `sum.golang.org`, `github.com` and `api.github.com`, with a loopback relay inside the area.
Telemetry and the auto-updater are off by environment.
The GitHub token handed to the area is fine-grained and limited to the hub's repositories; the operator's `gh` login never enters.
WebFetch and the `prowler` skill reach only these hosts.

### Stage 3: a broker for the remaining exits

A host-side process serving a fixed set of verbs and never a command line from the area: the landing deploy (it fetches `origin/main` into its own clone, checks the commit is the tip, builds with the host's Go and installs), `lym reed window` opening Konsole, and `lym hibernate request`.
`lym ide` is refused, since VS Code on the host would run git over repositories the area writes; the host runs no git over the area's repositories at all.

## What is not claimed

Isolation from a kernel exploit, which needs a virtual machine; that data in the area cannot leave through an allowed host; and that a landed change of lym itself cannot run on the host once deployed, which matters on this hub because it develops lym.
Landlock stays a possible inner layer once both machines run a kernel with ABI 9 and 10, and Claude Code deny rules in shuttle's settings are a cheap second line inside the area; the dedicated user, podman, systemd sandboxing and Claude Code's `/sandbox` inside lym runs are left out.
The report estimates the whole at five tasks and eighteen cards.

## Related

Note `creel-cross-hub-mail`: the inbox folder sits outside an area, so reading and writing it goes through the broker.

entries.title: Measure what Cortex XDR costs the test suites on OSL-1046
entries.brief: The 242 s fabricengine tier 1 against 37 to 41 s elsewhere is a machine difference no report has split
entries.body:
## Seen (operator, 2026-11-09)

Cortex XDR on OSL-1046 holds each new binary for about 10 s and scans each file a test creates, and fabricengine tests create many.
The shard report (`docs/research/speed/fabricengine-shards-2026-11-09/report.md`) put the 242 s one-process wall down to load, but the 2026-11-08 figure of 37 to 41 s was measured on another machine, so the gap is machine and Cortex, not load.
The package used 1.23 cores of 16 and `pmd` and `piud` were busy in nearly every sample.

## Idea

Separate the Cortex cost from the rest: the time a freshly built test binary waits before it runs, the time file creation takes with and without a scanned folder, and the fabricengine tier 1 wall with the repository and temp folders excluded from the scan, if the operator can have that changed.
The result says whether to cut tests, cut file and binary creation, or ask for an exclusion.

entries.title: Move a running task by hand-back and a fresh run, not a re-parent verb
entries.brief: The writer hands back what it knows, the run is cancelled, a new task under the new parent starts from that
entries.body:
## Seen

The study `docs/research/loom/reparent-running-task-2026-11-12.md` (commit `5e41ee2b`) finds that a verb moving a running task to another parent is feasible but wide:
two durable stores written by two modules with no atomic change, a narrow board write past the run lock,
an ancestry check on the new parent, and a cross-module tapestry run of its own.

## Idea (operator, 2026-11-15)

Moving a running task is rare, and a verb for it is clumsy for what it buys.
Instead, end the run and start a new one with more information:

1. The run's live writer writes everything it has learned to a hand-back file in its run records:
   what is done, the decisions taken, what is left, and where its commits are.
   The entry is held by the run and takes no body edit, so the file is the only place it can write.
2. The run is cancelled with `lym batten cancel`, which sets the entry back to `draft` and frees it.
   The archive tag keeps the run records, the hand-back and the commits, so the new run can read them.
3. The orch writes the hand-back into the entry's body, or into a new task under the new parent, and releases it.

What the design must settle:

- Whether the new run re-uses the old commits (a cherry-pick, which brings back the study's ancestry question) or only reads them.
- Whether this is a recipe step, a `lym batten` verb, or orch guidance alone.

The adopt redesign (`adopt-redesign`) has landed, and so has `run-fsm-tracked-records` (`27eefef6`, one run FSM over tracked records).
The project `adopt-build-resplit` has landed whole: its members `transition-push-takeover`, `machine-registry-holds-catchup`, `adopt-foreground` and `leftover-pairs-teardown` are in (`71d6ee1a`),
so the adopt work this note waited on is built.

entries.title: Single-repository hubs: records and board under refs/lym/, the layout known only to fabric
entries.body: Groups the entries filed from the Sketch `fabric-single-repo-mode`: single-repo-fabric-mode, single-repo-code-identity.

entries.title: Hardener campaign on fabric, one-repository layout
entries.brief: Hardener run on the one-repository part of fabric only
entries.body:
## Focus

Harden only the one-repository hub layout that 57015a52 added: one origin holds the code under `refs/heads/` and `refs/tags/`, and the records and board under `refs/lym/heads/` and `refs/lym/tags/`.
Everything else in fabric, the two-repository layout included, is out of scope, and no round is steered outside this focus.

Drive each of these live on a one-repository sandbox hub (`lym harden sandbox new --single-repo`), with real git and real `lym` verbs, and improvise scenarios beyond them:

- **Seeding**: `lym fabric clone --single-repo <url>` on an empty origin and on one with code only.
  The board ref is pushed last; kill or fail the push at each step and check that nothing on origin reads as a hub, the hub directory is gone and the records branch is restored.
- **Joining**: a second `lym fabric clone <url>` of a seeded origin takes the one-repository layout, gets the refspecs and `branch.main.merge refs/lym/heads/main`, and sees the board.
- **Refusals**: `--single-repo` on an origin that already holds a namespaced board, a records repository on the default branch, a second URL, or the old layout's `lym-bolt` branch or root `.lym-anchor`/`_lym`.
  Each refuses before creating anything and names its way forward.
- **Namespace leaks**: no records ref ever lands under plain `refs/heads/` or `refs/tags/` on origin, and the code store never fetches or pushes a records ref.
  Check every path: add, push, pull, replay, hand-over, teardown, archive, remote cleanup.
  The archive tag of a discarded task branch was seen in plain `refs/tags/` in a sandbox trial; confirm or refute it.
- **Two clones at once**: pushes and pulls from two clones of the same hub, a board write from each, a lease that loses.
- **Remote delete**: deleting a missing namespaced branch records no deletion; deleting a present one removes it under `refs/lym/heads/`.
- **Prime records branch**: `lym.primeRecordsBranch` is written once by the clone; a store without it fails closed with a way forward, and the orphan sweep keeps the branch.
- **Layout detection**: the records store's fetch refspec decides the layout; an unreadable remote config is an error, never read as two repositories.
- **Config read**: git's `@{u}` works on a namespaced branch, and `gitrepo`'s tolerant config read accepts `refs/lym/heads/<b>`.

Every finding states the repro steps that showed it.

entries.title: Autonomy mode: the parent orch settles every halt, operator only for severe halts and the beam merge
entries.brief: Parent orch settles all halts of a project or beam; operator reached only for a severe halt or a merge-ready beam PR
entries.body:
## Goal (operator, 2026-11-22)

An autonomy mode under which the run's parent orch receives every halt of every member run and settles it itself.
Whether a beam is autonomous is decided per beam: one beam may run autonomous while another beside it does not.
The operator is reached only in two cases:

1. A severe halt the orch cannot settle.
2. The beam is ready to merge: lym opens the beam's pull request ready for merge, then notifies the operator.

Wanted first in the Models hub on OSL-1046 and in loomyard.

## What was seen

Runs halt often for the operator: one halt per drift evaluation, one per pull request of a member task, and other parent-only stops.
Drift blocks are the largest share in recent runs.

## What exists

- Run agents put their questions to the parent orch (e55618bb).
- `code_review_ask_parent` and `judge_ask_parent` let the parent see and veto code review rounds and drift judge rulings (8998a865); a drift does-not-match ruling still stops the run.
- Halts reach the parent as batten and dobby notices, but the run then waits for a resume, a decision or `pr-continue` that the operator often gives.

## Open for the design

- Which halts the orch may settle, and how a halt is marked severe enough for the operator.
- How member PR review is handled under the mode: off, or reviewed by the parent.
- The setting: a per-beam switch, and whether a hub or the prime's root tasks can take it too; it sets the existing ask keys and the new halt routing.

entries.title: A stale records tracking ref blocks a cancelled slug from running again
entries.brief: OriginCodeTip reads a deleted records branch through an unpruned tracking ref; dobby refuses the start
entries.body:
## What was seen (2026-11-22)

`harden-fabricengine` was cancelled with `lym batten cancel --remove` on 2026-11-21 and released again after the hardener rebuild landed.
Dobby refused to start it three times: `the code tip 3a9f8d84 the run's last transition names is not on origin yet`, though 3a9f8d84 is on origin/main.

Cause: the records repository still held the remote-tracking ref `origin/harden-fabricengine-weft` of the cancelled run, while origin had deleted the branch.
`fabricengine.OriginCodeTip` reads that ref, finds the old run's last transition and judges its code tip missing.

Workaround: `git -C <hub>/loomyard-weft fetch --prune origin`, which also dropped two other stale refs.

## Expected

- `lym batten cancel --remove` and the remote cleanup drop the local remote-tracking ref of a deleted records branch, or the records fetch prunes.
- `OriginCodeTip` reads no records branch origin no longer holds, so a cancelled slug can run again.
- The refusal's way forward names the real cause, not a code push that will never land.

entries.title: Board README: beam marker, no empty sections, no Notes level
entries.brief: Declutter the rendered board README in a sampler session
entries.body:
## Goal (operator, 2026-11-22)

Make the rendered board README less cluttered, tried out with the operator in a sampler session:

- **Beam marker**: mark each project that has a beam, in its heading and in any project list.
- **No empty sections**: render no section, heading or table that holds no entry, such as a project's empty Tasks and Ready.
- **No Notes level**: drop the Notes heading above the type groups; Features, Bugs, Enhancements and the other type groups become sections of their own.

The session shows the operator renderings of the current board and keeps what the operator picks.

entries.title: Hardener rounds may run fabric verbs in their own sandbox hubs
entries.brief: The task-session fabric guard refuses hardener rounds the verbs they must drive on sandbox hubs
entries.body:
## What was seen (2026-11-22)

Round 1 of `harden-fabricengine` built a one-repository sandbox hub with `lym harden sandbox new --single-repo` and drove it live.
Every mutating `lym fabric` verb was refused from its round agent: add, push, pull, sync, reconcile, checkout, remove, clone and cleanup --apply.
The refusal is `sandboxedRoleRefusal` in `internal/fabriccli/roleguard.go`, which reads only the strand name, so it also refuses verbs run inside the round's own sandbox hub.
Seven of twelve charter items ended as could not verify: the join, the refusals, two clones, the remote delete, pair crash and rebirth, URL variations and every pair verb.

## Idea

Let a hardener round's agent run the mutating fabric verbs in a hub under its own sandbox root, `<worktree>/.lym/harden-sandbox`, and keep the refusal everywhere else.
The guard then checks the hub the verb resolves, not only the strand name, so a verb aimed at the real hub stays refused.

entries.title: Sampler session loads the language skills before it edits code
entries.brief: The sampler spec carries no language skills, so the sampler edits code without the skills of the repository's languages.
entries.body:
## What was seen (operator, 2026-11-22)

The sampler session of `readme-declutter` edited code without loading the language skills first, and the code it wrote was poor for it.

## Cause

`samplerengine.SessionSpec` (`internal/samplerengine/spec.go`) builds the sampler spec with no `Skills`, while darn, webster, weaver and the fixers pass the hub's `LanguageSkills`.
`spec_test.go` pins that the sampler spec carries no skills.

## Fix

The sampler session loads the language skills of the repository it works in before it edits code, the same way the darn writer gets them.
Which skills follow from the hub's languages, never a fixed language: a Go hub gets the Go skills, a C# hub the C# skills (operator, 2026-11-22).
Wire `LanguageSkills` from `loomcli/samplerwiring.go` into `SessionInputs` and onto the spec, and change the test to pin that the skills are carried.

entries.title: Hardener live check passes packages go can resolve
entries.brief: hardenLiveArgs passes bare internal/x paths, which go reads as std packages, so harden-live fails at setup every round.
entries.body:
## What was seen (harden-fabricengine, 2026-11-22)

The seed pass wrote `hardener.packages` as worktree-relative directories without `./`, such as `internal/fabricengine`.
`hardenLiveArgs` (`internal/loomcli/hardenwiring.go`) appends them verbatim to `lym gate test`, so go reads them as standard-library import paths:
`package internal/fabricengine is not in std`, then `[setup failed]` for each package.
The `harden-live` check after every fix round was red before any test ran, and the fixer looped on a gate no fix could clear.
The orch unblocked the run by rewriting the local layer with `./` prefixes.

## Fix

`hardenLiveArgs` passes each package as a directory path go reads as one: prefix `./` to a relative path that lacks it.
`CheckCampaign` already reads the packages as directories under the worktree root, so both forms stay valid in config.
A test pins that a bare `internal/x` reaches `gate test` as `./internal/x`.

entries.title: lym report convergence stays within bounded memory
entries.brief: convergence grew to 9.5 GB in two minutes over a four-week window and froze the machine.
entries.body:
## What was seen (Neve, 2026-11-22)

`lym report convergence --since 2026-10-20 --format markdown`, run from the prime, grew by about 2 GB every 15 seconds to 9.5 GB resident within two minutes.
Beside the hub's runs it filled the 16 GB user slice and its swap; the load reached 112 and the machine froze at 11:27 and needed a hard restart.
The `memsample` lines in the journal of boot `518480c4e3544695b00b6cff201b8af5` show the growth sample by sample.

## Cause

`readLandings` (`internal/reportengine/landings.go`) walks the whole board branch with no window, `src.Board.Log(src.BoardTip, gitrepo.LogQuery{})`: about 26 000 commits, since every board write is a commit.
`boardDoneAfter` and `labelsOf` then read `board.json` at board commits one by one, a git read each, through `tasksAt`.
`tasksAt` keeps every parsed board in `boardTasks` for the whole report and never drops one, so memory grows with the board's history.
Each `boardDoneAfter` call walks every board commit after its run opened, once per run, so the work grows with runs times board commits.

## Fix

Read the board history once, bounded by the report window, and keep only what the joins need:
per slug, the time its entry first reads done after a given point, and its labels at a landing.
No parsed board is held past the read of its commit.
A test pins the bound: the joins read each board commit at most once, and hold no board beyond the one being read.

## Sweep of the rest of reportengine (operator, 2026-11-22)

Go through every report in `internal/reportengine`, timing, cost, raddle and replies included, for the same pattern:
a git history walk with no window, a read per commit where one read would do, or a cache that keeps every parsed revision for the whole report.
Fix each place found in this run, and pin each fix with a test as above.

entries.title: The board README renderer carries tests for pure cosmetics
entries.brief: A renderer of board markdown carries no layout tests; delete the README goldens and keep only tests of behaviour other code relies on.
entries.body:
## Decision (operator, 2026-11-22)

Output only a human reads, such as the rendered README, gets no test of its layout or wording.
The general rule goes into `scribe:testing` through the scribe hub; this entry runs as darn light once that rule has landed.

## What to do

- Delete the README layout goldens in `internal/boardengine/render_test.go` and the heading parsing in `view_test.go`; do not move them to testdata files.
- Keep the tests of behaviour other code relies on, without pinning the layout: `RenderToDisk` rewriting a file in place and its manifest cleanup, and `board-data.js` holding each entry, which `board.html` reads.
- Sweep the repository for other renderers of human-read output carrying layout goldens, and delete those too.

## What was seen

In `readme-declutter` the format change touched about 200 lines of `render.go` and about 480 lines of `render_test.go`.
On main, `render_test.go` is longer than `render.go`: each run covered its format change with a new golden, and reviewers flag a change without a test.

entries.title: Orch remote control is off by default
entries.brief: lym turns on remote control for every orch it launches; it must stay off until the operator turns it on.
entries.body:
## What was seen (operator, 2026-11-22)

Bringing up the scribe hub's orch with `lym beam start` turned on Claude Code's remote control for it, because `internal/orchengine/template.yaml` ships `remote_control: true`.
The operator decides when a session gets remote control; lym must never turn it on by itself.

## Fix

- `remote_control` defaults to `false` in the orch template, so no hub gets remote control on any launch or resume unless its config turns it on.
- Every hub that has no explicit value takes the new default; ship the reinterpretation `PATTERN-config-layers` asks for a meaning change.
- The RC button of a pane stays the operator's way to turn it on for one agent.
- Check that no other launch path, such as a beam orch or a respawn, turns remote control on by its own default.
